text: What does the 1971 Liberation War refer to? It refers to the armed struggle in East Pakistan that led to the independence of Bangladesh after mass repression, resistance, and full-scale war.
Why did war break out in 1971? The refusal to transfer power after the 1970 mandate, escalating political deadlock, and military crackdown triggered armed conflict.
Who were the key actors in 1971? Bengali political leadership, freedom fighters, civilians, and external regional actors all shaped the course of the war.
Why is 1971 foundational to Bangladesh? It established sovereignty, national memory, and the core legitimacy of the modern Bangladeshi state.
1971 turned a denied democratic mandate into a war for national survival and independence.
source: Historical reflection on the Liberation War
